findings.finding: Inside the quarter (2026-09-10 Zagreb/Verne release) Pony.ai restated that it targets a global fleet of more than 3,500 robotaxis by YE2026 across 20+ cities, three weeks after the Q2 call. Against 1,975 at June 30, that implies ~1,500 additions in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The fleet target raise at Q1 2026 (3,000 to 3,500) came with a +3-4% day; the reaffirmation at Q2 came with -2.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The reaffirmation is public, so it is mostly priced. What is not priced is the Sep-30 fleet count: no company release between Aug 18 and Nov 16 gives a total fleet number (the 2026-11-16 Toyota bZ4X release gives none). If the market believed the target, the stock would not trade at 0.3x its mean target. This is inside what the company has already guided.
findings.independence: Shares its target with the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969302/000110465926098113/tm2623382d1_ex99-1.htm), so it is the same company claim restated, not independent evidence. The Toyota release of 2026-11-16 (https://blog.pony.ai/pony-ai-and-toyota-launch-fully-driverless-commercial-services-with-gen-7-bz4x-robotaxi/) adds a third Gen-7 model in driverless commercial service with ~1,000 units planned.

findings.finding: The next guide most likely holds or raises: H1 2026 robotaxi revenue of RMB140M (~$19.5M; Q1 ~$7.4-8.6M, Q2 $12.1M) already exceeded all of FY2025, the target was raised at Q1 from 3x to >3.5x 2025, and the CEO said at Q2 he is 'confident in our ability to exceed our full-year Robotaxi services revenues target'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raise of the robotaxi target came with an up day (+3-4%); the Q2 'confident to exceed' language came with -2.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The target and the confidence are public. If the market priced a raise, the stock would not have halved since the call. A formal raise, or a number for the robotaxi target, would be new. The risk is that the target needs H2 robotaxi revenue of roughly 2.5x H1, so a reaffirmation without a raise could read as stretched.
findings.independence: The Q2 release quote is the same source family (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969302/000110465926098113/tm2623382d1_ex99-1.htm), so it shares a document with the mid-quarter finding. Hesai's Q3 robotaxi lidar comment is independent and filed separately.

findings.finding: Pony's sole primary-lidar supplier Hesai reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-10. Its CFO said 'stronger shipments for robotaxis, robovans and humanoid robots helped offset weaker demand' from a lawnmower customer, and Hesai claims 62% of global robotaxi lidar. Total robotics lidar units still fell 35.6% q/q to 91,618, so the robotaxi strength is net of a large lawnmower drop.
findings.link: Hesai's AT128 is the primary lidar on all Pony Gen-7 robotaxis, four units per vehicle (Hesai release 2025-04-24, https://www.automotiveworld.com/news/four-at128-lidar-sensors-from-hesai-selected-as-primary-lidar-for-all-pony-ai-seventh-generation-robotaxis/). Pony is one of several robotaxi customers (Apollo Go, WeRide also use Hesai), so the comment is sector-level, not Pony-specific.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history of supplier reads on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Hesai's print came after Pony last spoke and is not in PONY's wire coverage. PONY fell ~19% from Nov 9 to Nov 17 despite it, so the market has not read it as a Pony fleet signal. It is a proxy: it confirms robotaxi lidar demand rose in Q3, but not Pony's own build count.
findings.independence: Hesai Q3 shipment data https://www.panabee.com/news/hesai-earnings-q3-2026 (shows the 35.6% q/q drop in robotics lidar overall). Independent of the Pony-sourced findings.

findings.finding: China resumed robotaxi licence approvals on or about 2026-07-23 after the nationwide freeze that followed the 2026-03-31 Apollo Go Wuhan outage. Q3 was therefore the first full quarter in which Pony could add permits for new vehicles and cities (it targets Changsha, Hangzhou and more Greater Bay Area cities).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: During the freeze Pony still grew its fleet from >1,700 (late May) to 1,975 (Jun 30); the Q2 print came with -2.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July, so mostly priced. The new part is how much of it shows up as Q3 fleet and city additions, which only the release will show. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Freeze reported by The Star / Bloomberg 2026-04-29 https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/04/29/china-suspends-autonomous-driving-permits-after-baidu-outage; Caixin on fleets expanding despite the pause https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-05-28/china-robotaxi-firms-expand-fleets-despite-regulatory-pause-102448697.html

findings.finding: Q2 GAAP net loss of $45.4M included a $33.4M fair-value gain on trading securities and a $25.0M impairment of long-term investment prepayments. The Q3 GAAP line can swing by tens of millions on those marks with no bearing on operations; non-GAAP net loss was a flat $44.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A narrower GAAP loss in Q2 did not prevent -2.9%; headlines on the 'H1 loss exceeding FY2025' circulated in November (trading-treff, 2026-11-15).
findings.why_not_priced: If the fair-value gain does not repeat, a wider GAAP headline loss could draw a negative headline on a name where loss headlines circulate. It has no path to guidance, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Trading-treff 2026-11-15 on the H1 loss narrative https://trading-treff.de/trading/pony-ai-aktie-halbjahresverlust-toppt-das-ganze-vorjahr

findings.finding: Cash burn is the line Earnings Whispers names as the skeptic's focus. Q2 free cash flow was -$76.2M (capex $32.2M) and cash and investments fell $45M q/q to $1,390.5M, roughly 4-5 years of runway at that rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 burn with a loss 'persisting' was cited in the -2.9% day (Yicai).
findings.why_not_priced: Runway is not at risk, so it is mostly priced. Fleet additions under the joint-fleet model are partner-funded, so Q3 capex may not scale with the fleet. A rise in burn would be the negative surprise, which is why the finding is sized small and negative.

baseline_tension: The findings lean up, which agrees with the call-side skew (-4.19) and so is partly priced. They cut against the run-up: the 20-day -25.6% and the last two sessions' heavy-volume selling around the founder lock-up expiry say holders are still exiting. The lean therefore stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: $39.1M vs an $83.4M outlier, 2 analysts): every finding capped at <=1.0; expectations finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0.

Rule 6 / core table (inside what was already guided): the Sep-10 fleet reaffirmation cut from +1.0 to +0.5 and the next-guide finding from +1.0 to +0.8; independence notes that they share the Q2 document.
Rule 7 (sign agrees with the call skew, so partly priced): positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; p_up 57 -> 56.
Rule 5 (proxy and absence): Hesai supplier read cut from +0.8 to +0.6, China permit resumption from +0.5 to +0.3, 'no fleet count released' from -0.5 to -0.3.

Rebuilt the base rate from confirmed releases (Q3'25 +5.9%, Q1'26 ~+3-4%, Q2'26 -2.9%) instead of the untrustworthy 6-K history; abs_move_pct 10 -> 9, still well above the 3-6% realised history because the stock is at lows with a lock-up just expired.
print_vs_bar_pct trimmed from 3.0 to 2.5 because Intelligent Solutions is lumpy (Q2 +4% y/y).
